content:
anna-runtime: heads up — repro of slab drift on long-context load with Mistral-GQA. kv page count climbs steadily after ~120k tokens, fragmentation ratio > 0.6 :eyes:

mike-eng: what does the allocation timeline look like? any correlation with kernel switches / batch boundaries?

anna-runtime: quick paste from the run: `replay --model=mistral-gqa --seq=160k --clients=8 --batch=auto`
```
kv_pages: 24k -> 37k over 2h
frag_ratio: 0.62
last_kernel_switch: 00:23:45 (mqa->gqa)
page_evicts/sec: 18
```

raj-sre: perf-bot alert earlier showed `kv_slab_util > 0.85` on that host, then we saw a short GC pause. Could be eviction bias where small slabs never coalesce.

perf-bot: alert: kv_slab_util exceeded threshold on node gpu-14 at 2612468200. sample: host_heap_map heatmap attached.

tess-ml: interesting — on MQA variants we saw kernel-select bouncing when sequence lengths in the batch vary widely; that likely creates micro-alloc churn and prevents nice coalescing. ran a deterministic trace, confirmed more kernel switches -> higher page churn.

mike-eng: can you share the trace/command to reproduce? I can run with slab compaction flag enabled.

anna-runtime: repro command above. also tried `--kv-compact-interval=60s --kernel-pin=gqa` — results: page growth slowed but overall latency slightly up (p50 +12ms). compaction reduced frag_ratio to ~0.45 after 30m.

raj-sre: notes from heap heatmap: lower-address slabs show steady residency, high-address slabs keep flipping. hypothesis: when kernel switches, new allocations prefer higher-address slabs; compaction doesn't move hot entries so reuse suffers.

perf-bot: from profiling: top cost during drift = `kv_page_coalesce: 34%`, `kernel_switch: 22%`, `memcopy`: 14%.

tess-ml: proposed next steps:
- run a canary with `--kernel-stability=prefer_last` to reduce switching (short-term)
- add an opportunistic compaction pass that targets high-address slabs only
- add telemetry for kernel-switch count per batch
- get a long-run with Llama and Qwen to see if pattern is model-specific

anna-runtime: opened a tiny PR to add `--compact-highaddr-only` (link: github.com/redwood/repo/PR/987) — put it on eng-runtime-canary for tomorrow. please +1 if you can validate the repro on your stacks.

mike-eng: will run across 4 nodes; will report numbers. if compaction helps, we can flip default for dedicated pools behind a flag. :thumbsup:

raj-sre: also let's add a short-term mitigation: lower slab allocation affinity for batches flagged >64k tokens so allocations scatter less. I'll file an infra ticket.

anna-runtime: thanks — logging expected results in the ticket. if anyone catches a weird host during canary, ping me immediately. :face_with_monocle:
